body:
The spec operates on code points, not bytes. By the time the HTML tokenizer sees these, the byte representation is irrelevant. You can encode them using any supported encoding.

This is the same as how HTML has always operated. You can already include Unicode in HTML tag names; it works fine. (Example: http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?saved=5782). The only thing this algorithm does is valid a string passed to it via a JavaScript API. (Again, no bytes in sight; only strings.)

I think that comment is fine as a valid example.

I understand you might not use Unicode in your custom tag names. I feel that's similar to a decision not to use Unicode in your text content, i.e. overly restrictive, but that's up to you.

You're also free to not use dots.

I'll close this as this appears to not be a bug report in the spec, but happy to continue discussing in the closed thread.
